mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE rising > 0.5 percentage points in one month) signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in one month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) from their prior month values signals a contraction in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending slowdown in manufacturing, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO declines during late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A rising CPI (CPIAUCSL increasing > 0.3% month-over-month) signals improving economic activity that boosts corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% m/m.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 900,000 units signals weak consumer confidence and reduced construction activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST < 900.0.

mechanism_narrative: A strong retail sales figure (RSAFS > 450,000 million dollars) indicates robust consumer spending that supports corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of periods when RSAFS > 450,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls.
